messages:
nina (CS): HarborField day0 quick sync — two blockers: KMS decrypt failing and audit logs not appearing in Splunk. /cc @mike @anya

deploy-bot: infra: harborfield/privnet apply complete. 2 hosts healthy. (deploy #12345) :white_check_mark:

mike (NetOps): can you paste the KMS error from your app logs?

harbor-admin (Customer): Error: `AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/aa-bb-cc`

anya (Security): Typical causes: key policy missing the redwood role ARN, or the IAM role lacks kms permissions. Add role to key policy and attach IAM policy allowing `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey`.

nina (CS): I'll DM a minimal policy snippet and a curl test for the Splunk HEC endpoint (port 8088).

harbor-admin (Customer): We added the role to the key policy but Splunk curl from the private agent times out. curl from public instance works.

mike (NetOps): Likely NAT/route table or SG egress. We'll re-associate the correct RT for priv subnet and ensure NAT-GW is used. ETA ~45m. Assigning: @mike

harbor-admin (Customer): NAT RT fixed and SG updated. Ran: `curl -v https://splunk.hec.harborfield.com:8088/services/collector/raw -H 'Authorization: Splunk <token>' -d 'ping'` -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK. Splunk shows test event.

harbor-admin (Customer): Re-ran private inference smoke -> 200 OK, no KMS errors. Cutover looks green.

anya (Security): Please enable multi-region CloudTrail to s3://harborfield-redwood-audit with log file validation and SSE-KMS. Default retention 90 days; requests for >365 days require procurement review and may affect renewal pricing.

nina (CS): I'll follow up in 3 days to confirm rotation schedule and retention settings. Flag renewal risk if they request >18 months retention. Closing unless new issues. :thumbsup:
